about: The systematic-review reproduction set (spec §10, Plan 5c Task 8): six PMC open-access systematic reviews, at least one per domain, each with the studies it included (from the review's own full text: DOI and PMID where it gives them, the title always, and the review's reference id) and its main conclusion. Selected live and model-free from Europe PMC, PubMed and OpenAlex; see each entry's note.

entries.title: Real-time computer aided colonoscopy versus standard colonoscopy for improving adenoma detection rate: A meta-analysis of randomized-controlled trials
entries.question: whether real-time computer-aided detection with deep convolutional neural networks during colonoscopy changes the adenoma detection rate compared with standard colonoscopy

pico.population: adults undergoing colonoscopy in randomised controlled trials
pico.intervention: real-time deep-learning computer-aided detection (CADe) during colonoscopy

included.title: Efficacy of real-time computer-aided detection of colorectal neoplasia in a randomized trial
Real-time automatic detection system increases colonoscopic polyp and adenoma detection rates: a prospective randomised controlled study
Detection of colorectal adenomas with a real-time computer-aided system (ENDOANGEL): a randomised controlled study
Study on detection rate of polyps and adenomas in artificial-intelligence-aided colonoscopy
Impact of a real-time automatic quality control system on colorectal polyp and adenoma detection: a prospective randomized controlled study (with videos)
Effect of a deep-learning computer-aided detection system on adenoma detection during colonoscopy (CADe-DB trial): a double-blind randomised study

main_conclusion.outcome: adenoma detection rate (CADe-assisted versus standard colonoscopy)

entries.note: Six RCTs, all with DOI and PMID; a single main outcome (adenoma detection rate) with a clear direction (RR 1.5 in favour of CADe); searched from inception to May 2020. Selection search (2026-11-09, model-free, the kernel's sources and query syntax, publication years inception–2020): europepmc: colonoscopy AND ("computer-aided" OR "computer aided" OR "artificial intelligence" OR "deep learning" OR "convolutional neural network") AND (adenoma OR polyp) AND (randomized OR randomised); pubmed: colonoscopy AND ("computer-aided" OR "computer aided" OR "artificial intelligence" OR "deep learning" OR "convolutional neural network") AND (adenoma OR polyp) AND (randomized OR randomised). 326 records, 295 after deduplication by DOI, PMID and title (budget 3,000); it finds 6 of the 6 included studies.

searches.query: colonoscopy AND ("computer-aided" OR "computer aided" OR "artificial intelligence" OR "deep learning" OR "convolutional neural network") AND (adenoma OR polyp) AND (randomized OR randomised)
colonoscopy AND ("computer-aided" OR "computer aided" OR "artificial intelligence" OR "deep learning" OR "convolutional neural network") AND (adenoma OR polyp) AND (randomized OR randomised)

provenance.included_from: the six RCTs the review analyses (Results: 'six prospective studies were included … [2–7]'; Table 1 study characteristics), references 2–7 of its reference list (Europe PMC full text: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7691740/fullTextXML)

entries.title: A meta-analysis of ozone effect on tooth bleaching
entries.question: whether ozone, alone or with hydrogen peroxide, changes tooth colour in in-office bleaching of vital teeth differently from conventional hydrogen peroxide bleaching

pico.population: patients receiving in-office bleaching of vital teeth in randomised clinical trials
pico.intervention: ozone, alone or combined with hydrogen peroxide

included.title: Effects of combining ozone and hydrogren peroxide on tooth bleaching: A clinical study
Color assessment after bleaching with hydrogen peroxide versus ozone: A randomized controlled clinical trial
Randomized controlled clinical trial on bleaching sensitivity and whitening efficacy of hydrogen peroxide versus combinations of hydrogen peroxide and ozone

main_conclusion.outcome: tooth colour change (ΔE) with ozone versus hydrogen peroxide bleaching

entries.note: A small, clearly reported review (four RCTs, Table 2, each with PMID) whose main conclusion has no difference as its direction (ozone is not superior to hydrogen peroxide), so the set covers that direction; searched up to May 2020. Selection search (2026-11-09, model-free, the kernel's sources and query syntax, publication years inception–2020): europepmc: ozone AND (bleaching OR whitening) AND (tooth OR teeth OR dental); pubmed: ozone AND (bleaching OR whitening) AND (tooth OR teeth OR dental). 190 records, 160 after deduplication by DOI, PMID and title (budget 3,000); it finds 4 of the 4 included studies.

ozone AND (bleaching OR whitening) AND (tooth OR teeth OR dental)

entries.note: An animal-physiology review: 24 studies listed in Table 1 (22 with DOI), one outcome (systolic blood pressure) with a clear direction (raised by fructose); studies published 2010–2022. Selection search (2026-11-09, model-free, the kernel's sources and query syntax, publication years 2010–2022): europepmc: TITLE_ABS:(fructose AND (hypertension OR "blood pressure") AND (rat OR rats)); pubmed: fructose[tiab] AND (hypertension[tiab] OR "blood pressure"[tiab]) AND (rat[tiab] OR rats[tiab]). 919 records, 470 after deduplication by DOI, PMID and title (budget 3,000); it finds 19 of the 24 included studies; not found by it: “Anti-hypertensive effect of abelmoschus esculentus (Okra) seed extracts in fructose-induced hypertensive rats” (no DOI); “Effect of the aqueous extract of Catharanthus roseus leaves against hypertention induced by fructose in rats” (10.22271/tpi.2020.v9.i9a.5170); “Effect of salix tetraspermaroxbugh on fructose induced hypertension in rats” (10.22159/ijpps.2017v9i9.18232); “An experimental model to induce metabolic syndrome in rats. entries.note: The food-chemistry review: experimental studies of trans-fatty-acid formation in heated oils, every included study with a DOI; its main conclusion has a clear direction above 200 °C (heating raises trans fatty acids; below 200 °C no appreciable change). 33 studies, a little over the preferred 30: PMC holds few chemistry systematic reviews that list their included studies. Selection search (2026-11-09, model-free, the kernel's sources and query syntax, publication years inception–2020): europepmc: TITLE_ABS:(("trans fatty acids" OR "trans fatty acid" OR "trans isomers" OR "trans fat" OR elaidic OR isomerization) AND (frying OR fried OR heating OR heated OR cooking OR thermal) AND (oil OR oils OR fat OR fats)); openalex: ("trans fatty acids" OR "trans isomers" OR elaidic) AND (frying OR "heat treatment" OR heating) AND ("vegetable oil" OR "edible oil" OR "frying oil" OR "cooking oil"). 2476 records, 2336 after deduplication by DOI, PMID and title (budget 3,000); it finds 26 of the 33 included studies; not found by it: “Formation of fatty acid geometrical isomers and of cyclic fatty acid monomers during the finish frying of frozen prefried potatoes” (10.1016/0963-9969(95)00024-0); “Changes in the characteristics and composition of oils during deep-fat frying” (10.1007/BF02523926); “Trans fatty acid production in deep fat frying of frozen foods with different oils and frying modalities” (10.1016/S0271-5317(00)00150-0); “Olive oil stability under deep-frying conditions” (10.1016/j.fct.2010.07.036); “Comparison of the stability of palm olein and a palm olein/canola oil blend during deep-fat frying of chicken nuggets and French fries” (10.1111/j.1365-2621.2011.02627.x); “Effects of frying oils’ fatty acids profile on the formation of polar lipids components and their retention in French fries over deep-frying process” (10.1016/j.foodchem.2017.05.100); “Thermal deterioration of virgin olive oil monitored by ATR-FTIR analysis of trans content” (10.1021/jf9012828).

pico.population: patients assessed for pulmonary hypertension with chest imaging
pico.outcome: diagnostic accuracy (AUC, sensitivity, specificity) for pulmonary hypertension

entries.note: A computing-method evaluation published in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence: 12 studies comparing machine-learning image interpretation with human reading, one outcome (diagnostic accuracy) with a clear direction (AI better); searched up to April 2025. Selection search (2026-11-09, model-free, the kernel's sources and query syntax, publication years inception–2025): europepmc: TITLE_ABS:(("pulmonary hypertension" OR "pulmonary arterial hypertension" OR "pulmonary artery pressure") AND ("artificial intelligence" OR "deep learning" OR "machine learning" OR "neural network")); pubmed: ("pulmonary hypertension"[tiab] OR "pulmonary arterial hypertension"[tiab] OR "pulmonary artery pressure"[tiab]) AND ("artificial intelligence"[tiab] OR "deep learning"[tiab] OR "machine learning"[tiab] OR "neural network"[tiab]). 753 records, 417 after deduplication by DOI, PMID and title (budget 3,000); it finds 12 of the 12 included studies.
